guides: Hi, I'm your guide. Every lesson in the Academy takes half a minute: I show you the real screens, and you can stop any time.
This is Home. Four ways to make a transcript at the top, your recordings below, your plan and the guide on the right.
Start with a file. MP3, MP4, WAV, any recording. Drop it here and the transcript is ready in minutes.
Start with a file. MP3, MP4, WAV, any recording. On a phone the plus button at the bottom opens this and the other three ways.
Instant speech. Press and talk. The words appear as you speak. Good for voice notes and dictation.
Meeting Recorder. Paste a Meet, Zoom or Teams invite. A bot joins the call, records it and writes the notes while you talk.
Transcribe from URL. A YouTube, Google Drive or Dropbox link. Nothing to download: paste it and go.

Speakers: Auto-detect is enough. I put a sample file in and switched Speaker identification on. Auto-detect counts the voices itself. Set a number only when you know it for sure: a wrong number puts two people in one voice.
Your turn. Press Start transcription with the sample, or drop your own file in its place. I count this lesson done the moment the upload starts.
Your turn. Press Start transcription with the sample, or tap to choose your own file. I count this lesson done the moment the upload starts.
Open the welcome recording. Every transcript is a row here. I made this one for you. Next opens it.
A recording. The transcript on the left, the tools above it, notes and outline on the right.
The title is yours. Click it to rename. Underneath: who made it, the folder, the speakers, the source and the length.
The title is yours. Tap it to rename. Underneath: who made it, the folder, the speakers, the source and the length.
Transcript and Summary. Transcript is every word, as it was said. Summary is the notes. We start on the transcript.
Click a timecode. The player jumps to that moment. While it plays, the words follow the voice.
Play, back, forward. Play starts where you are. The arrows step back or forward five seconds when you missed a word.
Set the pace. Half speed for a fast talker, double speed for a long call.
Hide the names. I switched Speakers off: the text reads as one clean block. Switch it back any time.
And the timecodes. Timestamps goes the same way. I put both back for you.
Back to the welcome recording. Same file as before. Next opens it.
Translate to. The transcript and the summary, in another language. Next opens the list.
Pick a language. Dozens of them. I'll take Spanish for this one.
Then press Translate. Spanish is picked. The Translate button next to it starts the work.
Then press Translate. Spanish is picked. On a phone the work starts the moment you pick a language.
A tab for each language. The Spanish transcript opens next to the original. Nothing is replaced: switch between them any time.
Copy or export it. Copy and Export now ask which language you want.
Edit transcript. A name, a term, a word the model misheard. Next turns the text into editing.
Click straight into the text. Every block is a field now. I put the cursor in the first one: type to fix it, like in any document.
Undo, reset, save. Undo steps back one change. Reset to original brings back what the model wrote. Save keeps it for everyone you share with.
Nothing is lost. Timecodes and speakers stay where they are. I leave editing now without saving.
Three voices, one unnamed. The app heard three people. Speaker 2 still needs a name. Next opens the list.
Rename, add, remove. Click a name to rename it. Remove a voice and its blocks go to someone else.
Rename, add, remove. Tap a name to rename it. Remove a voice and its blocks go to someone else.
Wrong name on one block. Click the name on that block and pick who really said it.
Wrong name on one block. Tap the name on that block and pick who really said it.
Two people in one block. Select the other person's words and pick their name. Only those words move.
The Summary tab. Notes written from the transcript: the decisions, the action items, what to remember.
Apply template. A template decides the shape: meeting notes, interview, lecture, action items. Pick one and the summary is rewritten in it.
All templates live here. Next takes you to the Templates page.
Templates. Every way a summary can be written, built in and yours.
Ready to use. Meeting notes, interviews, lectures and more. Star the ones you use and they stay close.
See it before you apply. Open a template to read its example summary. Then apply it from any recording.
Export. Everything about this recording, as files. Next opens the options.
Transcript. PDF, Word, plain text or subtitles. Choose whether speaker names and timestamps go in.
Summary, translation, audio. Each one is a switch. Turn on what you need, the rest stays out.
One click. Several files come as one zip. I close this for you now.
Share. Invite people by email or turn on a link. Next opens it.
Who can see it. Only the people you invite, or anyone with the link. They see the recording, its transcript and its summary.
Or just copy. No invite needed when you only want the words. Next opens Copy.
Or just copy. No invite needed when you only want the words. Copy is under More; Next opens it.
Transcript or summary. Either one goes straight to your clipboard, ready to paste into an email or a doc.
Shared with me. Recordings other people share with you land here.
Where recordings live. My Records, in the sidebar. Next takes you there.
My Records. Every recording you own, in one table. Tabs above, folders in the sidebar.
Recent, Starred, Shared, Trash. Star what you come back to. Trash keeps deleted recordings until you empty it.
Create a folder. One per client or project. Next opens the form.
A name and a colour. That is all a folder needs. It appears in the sidebar the moment you press Create.
Move recordings. Tick one or more and choose Move to folder. You can also pick a folder while uploading.
Share a whole folder. Hover a folder and press the people icon. Everyone invited sees every recording in it.
Where your calls live. Meetings, in the sidebar. Next takes you there.
Meetings. Your calendar with a recorder attached. Upcoming, past, and the calendars you connected.
Connect a calendar first. Google or Outlook, one sign-in. Until then this page is empty and the recorder cannot see your meetings.
Your calendar is connected. Every meeting from it lands here by itself. Another one connects from the Settings tab.
Auto-record. Each meeting has a switch. On, and the recorder joins by itself; the transcript is ready when the call ends.
Let the bot in. The recorder joins as a guest. When the host keeps a waiting room, someone has to let it in; otherwise nothing is recorded.
Or record one now. Paste any invite link from the Home page. Same recorder, no calendar needed.
Or from your computer. The desktop app records any call quietly in the background, with no bot in the room.
Quick Find. Searches what was said, not only the titles. Ctrl K opens it from anywhere.
Type what you remember. A name, a topic, a phrase. I typed one for you.
Every match, with its moment. Each result is a recording where those words were said. Click one to open it right there.
Every match, with its moment. Each result is a recording where those words were said. Tap one to open it right there.
Narrow it down. By folder, source, who recorded it or when.
Settings. Everything the recorder does by itself is set here, once a calendar is connected. Connect one first and the tab appears.
Settings. Everything the recorder does by itself is set on this tab.
Auto-record. Choose which meetings the recorder joins on its own: all of them, only the ones you host, or none.
After the call. Who gets the recap email and access to the recording: only you, or everyone who was invited.
Point at a block. When the mouse is over a block, a small bar appears on it. I show it for you.
Four things for one block. Highlight it, comment on it, share just that part, or copy its text.
Or select a few words. Select the words you need: only they get the highlight, the comment or the new speaker.
Trash. A deleted recording waits here. Nothing is gone at once.
Restore or delete for good. Open a row's menu: put it back where it was, or remove it forever.
What Free includes. The files you have used this month and the day the count resets.
What Free includes. This button opens your plan: what Free includes and what an upgrade adds.
When you need more. Start the trial or upgrade, right from this card.
When you need more. Start the trial or upgrade from the same button.
Audio and video files. This card takes any recording from your computer. Next opens it.
Audio and video files. The plus button takes any recording from your phone. Next opens it.
Drop a file here. Or click to choose one, then press Start transcription. Leave Speaker identification on Auto-detect unless you know the exact number. The step is done the moment the upload starts.
Drop a file here. Or tap to choose one, then press Start transcription. Leave Speaker identification on Auto-detect unless you know the exact number. The step is done the moment the upload starts.
Instant speech. Talk, and the words appear as you speak. Next opens it.
Say a few words. Press Start recording and talk for a few seconds. Press the red Stop and the step is done.
Meeting Recorder. A bot joins a Zoom, Meet or Teams call and writes the notes. Next opens it.
Paste the invite link. Copy it from the calendar invite, paste it here and press Transcribe now. The step is done when the recorder is on its way.
Transcribe from URL. YouTube, Google Drive, Dropbox and more. Next opens it.
Paste a link. Any public video or audio link, then press Start transcription. The step is done the moment it starts.
Meetings. Your calendar lives here. Next takes you there.
Connect Google or Outlook. Pick one and sign in. Your meetings then show up here by themselves.
A calendar is already connected. This step is done. Another calendar connects from the Settings tab.
Open the welcome recording. I made this one for you, so you can try it on real text. Next opens it.
Press Apply template. Pick a shape: meeting notes, interview, action items. The summary is rewritten in it.
Fix a word. At 1:02 the model wrote "lunch" for "launch". Press Edit transcript, fix the word and press Save.
Fix a word. At 1:02 the model wrote "lunch" for "launch". Open More, press Edit transcript, fix the word and press Save.
My Records. Folders live here. Next opens a new one.
Name it, press Create Folder. One folder per client or project. It shows up in your folders at once.
Three voices, one unnamed. Sam greets Priya in the first line, and Speaker 2 answers. Next opens the list.
Give Speaker 2 a name. Point at Speaker 2 and press the pencil. Type Priya, press Enter.
Give Speaker 2 a name. Press the pencil next to Speaker 2. Type Priya, press Enter.
Priority processing is on. You know your way around now. From here your files are processed first, even at peak times, with our best model.

welcome.speaker: Sam Rivera
welcome.text: Thanks for making time, Priya. Jordan runs production on our side and joins us today. The goal is to plan the customer interview series and agree how the recordings turn into notes.

welcome.speaker: Speaker 2
welcome.text: Perfect. We have twelve interviews booked between now and the end of the month, mostly on Zoom, a few in person. Nobody on my team has time to write them up by hand.

welcome.speaker: Jordan Lee
welcome.text: Then we record every call and send the files in a weekly batch. Each one comes back as a transcript, a summary and the action items, in the same shape every week.

welcome.speaker: Speaker 2
welcome.text: The same shape matters. My head of product reads these on the train, so a one-page summary with quotes is ideal.

welcome.speaker: Sam Rivera
welcome.text: That is a template. We set it once and every interview comes out as a one-pager with quotes. I'll send you the draft on Tuesday so you can tweak the sections.

welcome.speaker: Jordan Lee
welcome.text: One thing to decide: Fridays for the batch? The lunch is on the fourteenth, so the last batch lands the week before.

welcome.speaker: Speaker 2
welcome.text: Fridays work. And please keep the speaker names in, the quotes are worth nothing without who said them.

welcome.speaker: Sam Rivera
welcome.text: Done. Fridays it is, names stay in, draft template on Tuesday. I'll put the summary of this call in the shared folder tonight.
